title: The Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore East on 1971-04-29
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Tascam SS-R05 -> Samplitude Professional v11.2 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A superb soundboard capture of an incendiary 1971 show – crystal‑clear mix, booming organ and a smoking set featuring New Minglewood Blues, Hard to Handle, Alligator and China Cat > I Know You Rider.
ai_review.review: The multitrack soundboard source delivers astonishing depth and clarity, with Pig’s organ sitting front‑and‑center and the overall mix described as crisp and vivid. Musically the performance is fire‑hot – fans rave about the powerhouse renditions of New Minglewood Blues, Hard to Handle, Alligator and the seamless China Cat/​I Know You Rider, while the second set rolls with high energy and tight transitions.

ai_rating.rationale: Over two dozen reviews overwhelmingly praise both the show (energy, standout songs) and the recording (crisp, deep soundboard mix). Minor criticisms are few and do not outweigh the dominant enthusiasm.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Depth and clarity repeatedly noted; crisp mix with audible organ. A few listeners mention a slight bass leak or prefer an older source, but overall the recording is described as incredible.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Well‑paced with strong transitions, especially a seamless second set that builds momentum and delivers tight segues between tunes.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is highlighted as a ‘strut’ through China Cat and generally praised for its power and synchronicity.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir is noted for “slashing” through his parts and delivering solid rhythm guitar throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pig (organ) is described as clear, audible, ‘on fire’, and a key element of the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming receives compliments for being tight and fitting perfectly into the overall tightness of the performance.
